title: Little Candle, Little Table
goal: Read and spell two-syllable words ending in **consonant + le** (the sixth and last syllable type: candle, table, little).
review: ph, ch(/k/,/sh/), gh, and all earlier vowel-r/diphthong/aw teams

spell.sentence: Uncle put the purple candle on the little table.

listen.passage: A worker who checks their own work carefully before calling a job finished shows diligence — steady, careful effort, even on small details other people might not notice.

tier2.def: careful, steady effort, especially in checking details before finishing a job.
tier2.full: careful, steady effort, especially in checking details before finishing a job.

questions: Why might a customer trust a worker who shows diligence, even for a small job?

A.text: Maya's uncle made her a little purple table for her room. It was simple but sturdy, with four short legs and a smooth top. "You can put your candle, your puzzle, and your bottle of paint on it," her uncle said. Maya set a small candle in the middle, next to a puzzle piece shaped like an apple. Her little sister Zoe came in, saw the table, and let out a giggle. "Can I have a table too, Uncle?" Zoe asked. "Maybe a purple one for you as well," he said with a smile. That night, Maya sat at her little table and worked on her puzzle until she could hardly keep her eyes open.

B.text: At the repair shop, Bilal is asked to fix a wobbly table for a customer. One leg is a little shorter than the others, and the handle on the drawer has come loose. Bilal takes a sample of the wood to check the color match, then tightens the handle with a small tool. He turns the table upside down and adds a thin block under the short leg so it no longer wobbles. "It was a simple fix," Bilal tells the customer when she comes to collect it, "but I wanted to be sure it was sturdy before you took it home." The customer checks the table, gives it a gentle push, and smiles — no wobble at all.
